-> EvalOutcome:\n        \"\"\"Execute the per-eval lifecycle and return an ``EvalOutcome``.\n\n        Wraps :func:`run_eval` with logging proxies + a per-eval timeout\n        budget. The lifecycle itself is unchanged — every step still\n        runs through the FR-LC1 skeleton — so the status mapping rules\n        from ``D-0048/spec.md`` apply verbatim except for the TIMEOUT\n        branch this class adds.\n        \"\"\"\n\n        log = _JsonlLog(eval_id=spec.id, clock=self._clock)\n        timeout_sec = self._resolve_timeout(spec)\n\n        # Holders for the worker thread. ``outcome_holder`` is populated\n        # on clean return; ``exc_holder`` is populated when run_eval\n        # raised (KeyboardInterrupt / SystemExit, mainly — every other\n        # exception is folded into an ERRORED outcome by run_eval\n        # itself).\n        outcome_holder: dict[str, EvalOutcome] = {}\n        exc_holder: dict[str, BaseException] = {}\n\n        logged_home = _LoggingHomeProxy(self._home, log)\n        logged_executor = _LoggingExecutor(self._executor, log)\n        wrapped_expects = tuple(\n            _wrap_expect_with_log(c, index=i, log=log)\n            for i, c in enumerate(self._expect_callables)\n        )\n\n        # The wrapped ``deploy_hooks`` emits ``hooks_deployed`` once the\n        # underlying call returns; the spec does not require this event\n        # but it is the natural place to record that step 2 completed.\n        original_deploy = self._deploy_hooks\n\n        def logged_deploy(home_path: Path) -> None:\n            original_deploy(home_path)\n            log.emit(EvalRunner.EVENT_HOOKS_DEPLOYED, step=\"deploy_hooks\")\n\n        # ``on_teardown_error`` is invoked by ``_safe_teardown`` when\n        # teardown raises. _LifecycleState) -> tuple[EvalStatus, Optional[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Return ``(status, error_class)`` for the captured lifecycle state.\n\n    Encodes the status-mapping rules from ``artifacts/D-0048/spec.md``:\n\n    * Any captured harness exception -> ``ERRORED`` with the exception's\n      fully-qualified classname.\n    * Otherwise, all ``ExpectResult.passed == True`` -> ``PASS``.\n    * Otherwise -> ``FAIL``.\n\n    An empty ``expects`` tuple with no harness failure is ``PASS`` by\n    design (the eval ran cleanly and the manifest asked nothing of it).\n Build the per-Expect EvalContext now that we\n        # have stdout/stderr/exit_code/duration, then apply each\n        # callable in declaration order. A callable that raises folds\n        # into ERRORED with a partial ``expects`` tuple (whatever\n        # callables ran before the raise).\n        ctx = EvalContext.from_runner_state(\n            eval_spec=spec,\n            home=home,\n            run_dir=run_dir,\n            artifacts_dir=artifacts_dir,\n            stdout_path=stdout_path,\n            stderr_path=stderr_path,\n            transcript_path=transcript_path,\n            jsonl_paths=observed.jsonl_paths,\n            env=exec_ctx.env,\n            exit_code=observed.exit_code,\n            stdout=observed.stdout,\n            stderr=observed.stderr,\n            duration_sec=observed.duration_sec,\n            artifacts=observed.artifacts,\n        )\n\n        for callable_ in expect_callables:\n            try:\n                result = callable_(ctx)\n            except (KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit):\n                raise\n            except BaseException as exc:  # noqa: BLE001\n                state.record_harness_failure(step=\"assert\", exc=exc)\n                return _finalize(\n                    state=state,\n                    home=home,\n                    on_teardown_error=on_teardown_error,\n                    keep_home_on_pass=keep_home_on_pass,\n                )\n            state.record_expect(result)\n\n        return _finalize(\n            state=state,\n            home=home,\n            on_teardown_error=on_teardown_error,\n            keep_home_on_pass=keep_home_on_pass,\n        )\n\n    except (KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit):\n        # NFR-REL1 contract: cooperative cancellation. ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # Public surface\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    def run(self, spec: EvalSpec) -> EvalOutcome:\n        \"\"\"Execute the per-eval lifecycle and return an ``EvalOutcome``.\n\n        Wraps :func:`run_eval` with logging proxies + a per-eval timeout\n        budget. The lifecycle itself is unchanged — every step still\n        runs through the FR-LC1 skeleton — so the status mapping rules\n        from ``D-0048/spec.md`` apply verbatim except for the TIMEOUT\n        branch this class adds.\n\n        When a :class:`CancellationToken` is wired (NFR-REL1 / T03.07)\n        and the token is already cancelled at entry, the runner skips\n        the lifecycle entirely and returns an ``INTERRUPTED`` outcome.\n        Cancellations that arrive mid-flight are observed cooperatively\n        through the orchestrator (T03.15); the runner itself records\n        ``INTERRUPTED`` if the worker raises ``KeyboardInterrupt``\n        (matching the FR-LC1 skeleton's re-raise behaviour) only when a\n        cancellation_token is wired, otherwise propagation is preserved.\n        \"\"\"\n\n        log = _JsonlLog(eval_id=spec.id, clock=self._clock)\n        timeout_sec = self._resolve_timeout(spec)\n\n        # NFR-REL1: cooperative cancellation. If the signal handler has\n        # already flipped the token before we even start the worker,\n        # return INTERRUPTED immediately so the orchestrator does not\n        # waste a HomeIsolation setup on an eval whose result will be\n        # discarded anyway.\n        if self._cancellation_token is not None and self._cancellation_token.is_cancelled():\n            return self._make_interrupted_outcome(spec=spec, log=log)\n\n        # Holders for the worker thread. ``outcome_holder`` is populated\n        # on clean return; ``exc_holder`` is populated when run_eval\n        # raised (KeyboardInterrupt / SystemExit, mainly — every other\n        # exception is folded into an ERRORED outcome by run_eval\n        # itself).\n        outcome_holder: dict[str, EvalOutcome] = {}\n        exc_holder: dict[str, BaseException] = {}\n\n        logged_home = _LoggingHomeProxy(self._home, log)\n        logged_executor = _LoggingExecutor(self._executor, log)\n        wrapped_expects = tuple(\n            _wrap_expect_with_log(c, index=i, log=log)\n            for i, c in enumerate(self._expect_callables)\n        )\n\n        # The wrapped ``deploy_hooks`` emits ``hooks_deployed`` once the\n        # underlying call returns; the spec does not require this event\n        # but it is the natural place to record that step 2 completed.\n        original_deploy = self._deploy_hooks\n\n        def logged_deploy(home_path: Path) -> None:\n            original_deploy(home_path)\n            log.emit(EvalRunner.EVENT_HOOKS_DEPLOYED, step=\"deploy_hooks\")\n\n        # ``on_teardown_error`` is invoked by ``_safe_teardown`` when\n        # teardown raises. The proxy already logs the failure via\n        # ``EVENT_TEARDOWN_ERROR``; the callback is a no-op so the\n        # caller-injected behaviour (preserved by FR-LC1) keeps working\n        # if a future caller wires one through ``EvalRunner``.\n        def on_teardown_error(_exc: BaseException) -> None:\n            return None\n\n        def worker() -> None:\n            try:\n                outcome_holder[\"result\"] = run_eval(\n                    spec,\n                    home=logged_home,  # type: ignore[arg-type]  # duck-typed proxy\n                    config=self._config,\n                    run_dir=self._run_dir,\n                    artifacts_dir=self._artifacts_dir,\n                    stdout_path=self._stdout_path,\n                    stderr_path=self._stderr_path,\n                    transcript_path=self._transcript_path,\n                    executor=logged_executor,  # type: ignore[arg-type]  # duck-typed proxy\n                    expect_callables=wrapped_expects,\n                    deploy_hooks=logged_deploy,\n                    on_teardown_error=on_teardown_error,\n                    keep_home_on_pass=self._keep_home_on_pass,\n                )\n            except BaseException as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — captured for re-raise\n                exc_holder[\"exc\"] = exc\n\n        # ``daemon=True`` so a hung worker cannot block process exit.\n        # NFR-REL1 (T03.07) wires the PtyDriver kill + zombie reap that\n        # makes a hung worker rare in production.\n        thread = threading.Thread(\n            target=worker,\n            name=f\"EvalRunner[{spec.id}]\",\n            daemon=True,\n        )\n        thread.start()\n        thread.join(timeout=timeout_sec)\n\n        if thread.is_alive():\n            return self._handle_timeout(spec=spec, log=log, timeout_sec=timeout_sec)\n\n        # Worker returned. _LifecycleState) -> tuple[EvalStatus, Optional[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Return ``(status, error_class)`` for the captured lifecycle state.\n\n    Encodes the status-mapping rules from ``artifacts/D-0048/spec.md``:\n\n    * Any captured harness exception -> ``ERRORED`` with the exception's\n      fully-qualified classname.\n    * Otherwise, all ``ExpectResult.passed == True`` -> ``PASS``.\n    * Otherwise -> ``FAIL``.\n\n    An empty ``expects`` tuple with no harness failure is ``PASS`` by\n    design (the eval ran cleanly and the manifest asked nothing of it).\n If the signal handler has\n        # already flipped the token before we even start the worker,\n        # return INTERRUPTED immediately so the orchestrator does not\n        # waste a HomeIsolation setup on an eval whose result will be\n        # discarded anyway.\n        if self._cancellation_token is not None and self._cancellation_token.is_cancelled():\n            return self._make_interrupted_outcome(spec=spec, log=log)\n\n        # Holders for the worker thread. ``outcome_holder`` is populated\n        # on clean return; ``exc_holder`` is populated when run_eval\n        # raised (KeyboardInterrupt / SystemExit, mainly — every other\n        # exception is folded into an ERRORED outcome by run_eval\n        # itself).\n        outcome_holder: dict[str, EvalOutcome] = {}\n        exc_holder: dict[str, BaseException] = {}\n\n        logged_home = _LoggingHomeProxy(self._home, log)\n        logged_executor = _LoggingExecutor(self._executor, log)\n        wrapped_expects = tuple(\n            _wrap_expect_with_log(c, index=i, log=log)\n            for i, c in enumerate(self._expect_callables)\n        )\n\n        # The wrapped ``deploy_hooks`` emits ``hooks_deployed`` once the\n        # underlying call returns; the spec does not require this event\n        # but it is the natural place to record that step 2 completed.\n        original_deploy = self._deploy_hooks\n\n        def logged_deploy(home_path: Path) -> None:\n            original_deploy(home_path)\n            log.emit(EvalRunner.EVENT_HOOKS_DEPLOYED, step=\"deploy_hooks\")\n\n        # ``on_teardown_error`` is invoked by ``_safe_teardown`` when\n        # teardown raises. Build the per-Expect EvalContext now that we\n        # have stdout/stderr/exit_code/duration, then apply each\n        # callable in declaration order. A callable that raises folds\n        # into ERRORED with a partial ``expects`` tuple (whatever\n        # callables ran before the raise).\n        ctx = EvalContext.from_runner_state(\n            eval_spec=spec,\n            home=home,\n            run_dir=run_dir,\n            artifacts_dir=artifacts_dir,\n            stdout_path=stdout_path,\n            stderr_path=stderr_path,\n            transcript_path=transcript_path,\n            jsonl_paths=observed.jsonl_paths,\n            env=exec_ctx.env,\n            exit_code=observed.exit_code,\n            stdout=observed.stdout,\n            stderr=observed.stderr,\n            duration_sec=observed.duration_sec,\n            artifacts=observed.artifacts,\n        )\n\n        for callable_ in expect_callables:\n            try:\n                result = callable_(ctx)\n            except (KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit):\n                raise\n            except BaseException as exc:  # noqa: BLE001\n                state.record_harness_failure(step=\"assert\", exc=exc)\n                return _finalize(\n                    state=state,\n                    home=home,\n                    on_teardown_error=on_teardown_error,\n                    keep_home_on_pass=keep_home_on_pass,\n                )\n            state.record_expect(result)\n\n        return _finalize(\n            state=state,\n            home=home,\n            on_teardown_error=on_teardown_error,\n            keep_home_on_pass=keep_home_on_pass,\n        )\n\n    except (KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit):\n        # NFR-REL1 contract: cooperative cancellation. ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # Public surface\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    def run(self, spec: EvalSpec) -> EvalOutcome:\n        \"\"\"Execute the per-eval lifecycle and return an ``EvalOutcome``.\n\n        Wraps :func:`run_eval` with logging proxies + a per-eval timeout\n        budget. The lifecycle itself is unchanged — every step still\n        runs through the FR-LC1 skeleton — so the status mapping rules\n        from ``D-0048/spec.md`` apply verbatim except for the TIMEOUT\n        branch this class adds.\n\n        When a :class:`CancellationToken` is wired (NFR-REL1 / T03.07)\n        and the token is already cancelled at entry, the runner skips\n        the lifecycle entirely and returns an ``INTERRUPTED`` outcome.\n        Cancellations that arrive mid-flight are observed cooperatively\n        through the orchestrator (T03.15); the runner itself records\n        ``INTERRUPTED`` if the worker raises ``KeyboardInterrupt``\n        (matching the FR-LC1 skeleton's re-raise behaviour) only when a\n        cancellation_token is wired, otherwise propagation is preserved.\n        \"\"\"\n\n        log = _JsonlLog(eval_id=spec.id, clock=self._clock)\n        timeout_sec = self._resolve_timeout(spec)\n\n        # NFR-REL1: cooperative cancellation. If the signal handler has\n        # already flipped the token before we even start the worker,\n        # return INTERRUPTED immediately so the orchestrator does not\n        # waste a HomeIsolation setup on an eval whose result will be\n        # discarded anyway.\n        if self._cancellation_token is not None and self._cancellation_token.is_cancelled():\n            return self._make_interrupted_outcome(spec=spec, log=log)\n\n        # Holders for the worker thread. ``outcome_holder`` is populated\n        # on clean return; ``exc_holder`` is populated when run_eval\n        # raised (KeyboardInterrupt / SystemExit, mainly — every other\n        # exception is folded into an ERRORED outcome by run_eval\n        # itself).\n        outcome_holder: dict[str, EvalOutcome] = {}\n        exc_holder: dict[str, BaseException] = {}\n\n        logged_home = _LoggingHomeProxy(self._home, log)\n        logged_executor = _LoggingExecutor(self._executor, log)\n        wrapped_expects = tuple(\n            _wrap_expect_with_log(c, index=i, log=log)\n            for i, c in enumerate(self._expect_callables)\n        )\n\n        # The wrapped ``deploy_hooks`` emits ``hooks_deployed`` once the\n        # underlying call returns; the spec does not require this event\n        # but it is the natural place to record that step 2 completed.\n        original_deploy = self._deploy_hooks\n\n        def logged_deploy(home_path: Path) -> None:\n            original_deploy(home_path)\n            log.emit(EvalRunner.EVENT_HOOKS_DEPLOYED, step=\"deploy_hooks\")\n\n        # ``on_teardown_error`` is invoked by ``_safe_teardown`` when\n        # teardown raises. The proxy already logs the failure via\n        # ``EVENT_TEARDOWN_ERROR``; the callback is a no-op so the\n        # caller-injected behaviour (preserved by FR-LC1) keeps working\n        # if a future caller wires one through ``EvalRunner``.\n        def on_teardown_error(_exc: BaseException) -> None:\n            return None\n\n        def worker() -> None:\n            try:\n                outcome_holder[\"result\"] = run_eval(\n                    spec,\n                    home=logged_home,  # type: ignore[arg-type]  # duck-typed proxy\n                    config=self._config,\n                    run_dir=self._run_dir,\n                    artifacts_dir=self._artifacts_dir,\n                    stdout_path=self._stdout_path,\n                    stderr_path=self._stderr_path,\n                    transcript_path=self._transcript_path,\n                    executor=logged_executor,  # type: ignore[arg-type]  # duck-typed proxy\n                    expect_callables=wrapped_expects,\n                    deploy_hooks=logged_deploy,\n                    on_teardown_error=on_teardown_error,\n                    keep_home_on_pass=self._keep_home_on_pass,\n                )\n            except BaseException as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — captured for re-raise\n                exc_holder[\"exc\"] = exc\n\n        # ``daemon=True`` so a hung worker cannot block process exit.\n        # NFR-REL1 (T03.07) wires the PtyDriver kill + zombie reap that\n        # makes a hung worker rare in production.\n        thread = threading.Thread(\n            target=worker,\n            name=f\"EvalRunner[{spec.id}]\",\n            daemon=True,\n        )\n        thread.start()\n        thread.join(timeout=timeout_sec)\n\n        if thread.is_alive():\n            return self._handle_timeout(spec=spec, log=log, timeout_sec=timeout_sec)\n\n        # Worker returned. Either run_eval produced an outcome or raised\n        # an interrupt; the latter must propagate to the orchestrator so\n        # NFR-REL1 can mark INTERRUPTED. Flush the JSONL log first so\n        # the partial events survive the re-raise.\n        if \"exc\" in exc_holder:\n            exc = exc_holder[\"exc\"]\n            # NFR-REL1 (T03.07): when a cancellation token is wired, the\n            # runner converts a worker-thread KeyboardInterrupt /\n            # SystemExit directly into an ``INTERRUPTED`` outcome so the\n            # orchestrator's ThreadPoolExecutor + as_completed loop never\n            # has to translate an exception into a status. Without a\n            # token, propagation is preserved verbatim so the FR-LC1\n            # contract (and the existing ``test_runner_class.py`` AC4\n            # case) stays unchanged.\n            if (\n                self._cancellation_token is not None\n                and isinstance(exc, (KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit))\n            ):\n                self._cancellation_token.cancel()\n                return self._make_interrupted_outcome(spec=spec, log=log)\n            self._flush_log(log)\n            raise exc\n\n        outcome = outcome_holder[\"result\"]\n        # Record the terminal classification so post-mortem tooling can\n        # tell whether the run ended cleanly or was reclassified.\n        log.emit(\n            EvalRunner.EVENT_OUTCOME,\n            step=\"outcome\",\n            extra={\n                \"status\": outcome.status,\n                \"duration_sec\": outcome.duration_sec,\n                \"error_class\": outcome.error_class,\n            },\n        )\n        self._flush_log(log)\n        return outcome\n\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # Internals\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    def _resolve_timeout(self, spec: EvalSpec) -> Optional[float]:\n        \"\"\"Return the resolved per-eval timeout, or ``None`` for unbounded.\n\n        ``spec.timeout_sec`` takes precedence; if absent or 0 the\n        runner falls back to ``default_timeout_sec``. ``0`` is treated\n        as \"use the default\" rather than \"no timeout\" because a literal\n        zero would always fire and is never useful in practice.\n        \"\"\"\n        spec_timeout = spec.timeout_sec\n        if spec_timeout is not None and spec_timeout > 0:\n            return float(spec_timeout)\n        if self._default_timeout_sec is not None and self._default_timeout_sec > 0:\n            return float(self._default_timeout_sec)\n        return None\n\n    def _handle_timeout(\n        self,\n        *,\n        spec: EvalSpec,\n        log: _JsonlLog,\n        timeout_sec: Optional[float],\n    ) -> EvalOutcome:\n        \"\"\"Emit timeout events, attempt best-effort teardown, return outcome.\n\n        NFR-REL1 (T03.07) extends the T03.05 timeout path with a\n        subprocess kill + zombie reap step: if the wired executor\n        exposes a ``cancel()`` method (the production\n        ``ClaudeProcessAdapter`` + ``PtyDriver`` does), the runner calls\n        it from the main thread so the PtyDriver child terminates and\n        ``wait()`` reaps the zombie before the orchestrator collects\n        the next outcome. ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # Public surface\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    def run(self, spec: EvalSpec) -> EvalOutcome:\n        \"\"\"Execute the per-eval lifecycle and return an ``EvalOutcome``.\n\n        Wraps :func:`run_eval` with logging proxies + a per-eval timeout\n        budget. The lifecycle itself is unchanged — every step still\n        runs through the FR-LC1 skeleton — so the status mapping rules\n        from ``D-0048/spec.md`` apply verbatim except for the TIMEOUT\n        branch this class adds.\n\n        When a :class:`CancellationToken` is wired (NFR-REL1 / T03.07)\n        and the token is already cancelled at entry, the runner skips\n        the lifecycle entirely and returns an ``INTERRUPTED`` outcome.\n        Cancellations that arrive mid-flight are observed cooperatively\n        through the orchestrator (T03.15); the runner itself records\n        ``INTERRUPTED`` if the worker raises ``KeyboardInterrupt``\n        (matching the FR-LC1 skeleton's re-raise behaviour) only when a\n        cancellation_token is wired, otherwise propagation is preserved.\n        \"\"\"\n\n        log = _JsonlLog(eval_id=spec.id, clock=self._clock)\n        timeout_sec = self._resolve_timeout(spec)\n\n        # NFR-REL1: cooperative cancellation. If the signal handler has\n        # already flipped the token before we even start the worker,\n        # return INTERRUPTED immediately so the orchestrator does not\n        # waste a HomeIsolation setup on an eval whose result will be\n        # discarded anyway.\n        if self._cancellation_token is not None and self._cancellation_token.is_cancelled():\n            return self._make_interrupted_outcome(spec=spec, log=log)\n\n        # Holders for the worker thread. ``outcome_holder`` is populated\n        # on clean return; ``exc_holder`` is populated when run_eval\n        # raised (KeyboardInterrupt / SystemExit, mainly — every other\n        # exception is folded into an ERRORED outcome by run_eval\n        # itself).\n        outcome_holder: dict[str, EvalOutcome] = {}\n        exc_holder: dict[str, BaseException] = {}\n\n        logged_home = _LoggingHomeProxy(self._home, log)\n        logged_executor = _LoggingExecutor(self._executor, log)\n        wrapped_expects = tuple(\n            _wrap_expect_with_log(c, index=i, log=log)\n            for i, c in enumerate(self._expect_callables)\n        )\n\n        # The wrapped ``deploy_hooks`` emits ``hooks_deployed`` once the\n        # underlying call returns; the spec does not require this event\n        # but it is the natural place to record that step 2 completed.\n        original_deploy = self._deploy_hooks\n\n        def logged_deploy(home_path: Path) -> None:\n            original_deploy(home_path)\n            log.emit(EvalRunner.EVENT_HOOKS_DEPLOYED, step=\"deploy_hooks\")\n\n        # ``on_teardown_error`` is invoked by ``_safe_teardown`` when\n        # teardown raises. The proxy already logs the failure via\n        # ``EVENT_TEARDOWN_ERROR``; the callback is a no-op so the\n        # caller-injected behaviour (preserved by FR-LC1) keeps working\n        # if a future caller wires one through ``EvalRunner``.\n        def on_teardown_error(_exc: BaseException) -> None:\n            return None\n\n        def worker() -> None:\n            try:\n                outcome_holder[\"result\"] = run_eval(\n                    spec,\n                    home=logged_home,  # type: ignore[arg-type]  # duck-typed proxy\n                    config=self._config,\n                    run_dir=self._run_dir,\n                    artifacts_dir=self._artifacts_dir,\n                    stdout_path=self._stdout_path,\n                    stderr_path=self._stderr_path,\n                    transcript_path=self._transcript_path,\n                    executor=logged_executor,  # type: ignore[arg-type]  # duck-typed proxy\n                    expect_callables=wrapped_expects,\n                    deploy_hooks=logged_deploy,\n                    on_teardown_error=on_teardown_error,\n                    keep_home_on_pass=self._keep_home_on_pass,\n                )\n            except BaseException as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — captured for re-raise\n                exc_holder[\"exc\"] = exc\n\n        # ``daemon=True`` so a hung worker cannot block process exit.\n        # NFR-REL1 (T03.07) wires the PtyDriver kill + zombie reap that\n        # makes a hung worker rare in production.\n        thread = threading.Thread(\n            target=worker,\n            name=f\"EvalRunner[{spec.id}]\",\n            daemon=True,\n        )\n        thread.start()\n        thread.join(timeout=timeout_sec)\n\n        if thread.is_alive():\n            return self._handle_timeout(spec=spec, log=log, timeout_sec=timeout_sec)\n\n        # Worker returned. Either run_eval produced an outcome or raised\n        # an interrupt; the latter must propagate to the orchestrator so\n        # NFR-REL1 can mark INTERRUPTED. Flush the JSONL log first so\n        # the partial events survive the re-raise.\n        if \"exc\" in exc_holder:\n            exc = exc_holder[\"exc\"]\n            # NFR-REL1 (T03.07): when a cancellation token is wired, the\n            # runner converts a worker-thread KeyboardInterrupt /\n            # SystemExit directly into an ``INTERRUPTED`` outcome so the\n            # orchestrator's ThreadPoolExecutor + as_completed loop never\n            # has to translate an exception into a status. Without a\n            # token, propagation is preserved verbatim so the FR-LC1\n            # contract (and the existing ``test_runner_class.py`` AC4\n            # case) stays unchanged.\n            if (\n                self._cancellation_token is not None\n                and isinstance(exc, (KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit))\n            ):\n                self._cancellation_token.cancel()\n                return self._make_interrupted_outcome(spec=spec, log=log)\n            self._flush_log(log)\n            raise exc\n\n        outcome = outcome_holder[\"result\"]\n        # Record the terminal classification so post-mortem tooling can\n        # tell whether the run ended cleanly or was reclassified.\n        log.emit(\n            EvalRunner.EVENT_OUTCOME,\n            step=\"outcome\",\n            extra={\n                \"status\": outcome.status,\n                \"duration_sec\": outcome.duration_sec,\n                \"error_class\": outcome.error_class,\n            },\n        )\n        self._flush_log(log)\n        return outcome\n\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # Internals\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    def _resolve_timeout(self, spec: EvalSpec) -> Optional[float]:\n        \"\"\"Return the resolved per-eval timeout, or ``None`` for unbounded.\n\n        ``spec.timeout_sec`` takes precedence; if absent or 0 the\n        runner falls back to ``default_timeout_sec``. ``0`` is treated\n        as \"use the default\" rather than \"no timeout\" because a literal\n        zero would always fire and is never useful in practice.\n        \"\"\"\n        spec_timeout = spec.timeout_sec\n        if spec_timeout is not None and spec_timeout > 0:\n            return float(spec_timeout)\n        if self._default_timeout_sec is not None and self._default_timeout_sec > 0:\n            return float(self._default_timeout_sec)\n        return None\n\n    def _handle_timeout(\n        self,\n        *,\n        spec: EvalSpec,\n        log: _JsonlLog,\n        timeout_sec: Optional[float],\n    ) -> EvalOutcome:\n        \"\"\"Emit timeout events, attempt best-effort teardown, return outcome.\n\n        NFR-REL1 (T03.07) extends the T03.05 timeout path with a\n        subprocess kill + zombie reap step: if the wired executor\n        exposes a ``cancel()`` method (the production\n        ``ClaudeProcessAdapter`` + ``PtyDriver`` does), the runner calls\n        it from the main thread so the PtyDriver child terminates and\n        ``wait()`` reaps the zombie before the orchestrator collects\n        the next outcome. Failure is swallowed because the TIMEOUT\n        outcome must always return cleanly; the JSONL log records the\n        cancel attempt.\n        \"\"\"\n        budget = float(timeout_sec) if timeout_sec is not None else 0.0\n        log.emit(\n            EvalRunner.EVENT_TIMEOUT_FIRED,\n            step=\"timeout\",\n            extra={\"timeout_sec\": budget},\n        )\n\n        # NFR-REL1: kill the executor's subprocess + reap zombie before\n        # we attempt teardown. Documented on D-0050/spec.md.\n        self._cancel_executor(log=log, reason=\"timeout\")\n\n        log.emit(\n            EvalRunner.EVENT_TEARDOWN_STARTED,\n            step=\"teardown\",\n            extra={\"keep\": True},\n        )\n        try:\n            # The worker may still hold references to the HomeIsolation\n            # instance; HomeIsolation.teardown is idempotent enough that\n            # a main-thread call is safe even if the worker is mid-step.\n            # Failures are swallowed so the TIMEOUT outcome always\n            # returns cleanly.\n            if getattr(self._home, \"is_set_up\", False):\n                self._home.teardown(keep=True)\n        except BaseException as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — best-effort\n            cls = type(exc)\n            log.emit(\n                EvalRunner.EVENT_TEARDOWN_ERROR,\n                step=\"teardown\",\n                extra={\n                    \"error_class\": f\"{cls.__module__}.{cls.__qualname__}\",\n                    \"message\": str(exc),\n                },\n            )\n\n        outcome = EvalOutcome(\n            eval_id=spec.id,\n            title=spec.title,\n            status=\"TIMEOUT\",\n            duration_sec=budget,\n            expects=(),\n            skip_reason=None,\n            skip_flag_triggered=None,\n            artifacts={},\n            error_class=\"builtins.TimeoutError\",\n        )\n        log.emit(\n            EvalRunner.EVENT_OUTCOME,\n            step=\"outcome\",\n            extra={\n                \"status\": outcome.status,\n                \"duration_sec\": outcome.duration_sec,\n                \"error_class\": outcome.error_class,\n            },\n        )\n        self._flush_log(log)\n        return outcome\n\n    def _cancel_executor(self, *, log: _JsonlLog, reason: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Best-effort PtyDriver kill + zombie reap on the wired executor.\n\n        The production executor (``ClaudeProcessAdapter`` driving a\n        ``PtyDriver``) exposes a ``cancel()`` method that calls\n        ``PtyDriver.terminate(force=True)`` followed by ``close()`` so\n        the child process is signalled and ``wait()`` reaps the\n        resulting zombie. Goal\n\nProvide the *cancellation primitives* the harness needs so that:\n\n* Pressing `Ctrl-C` (SIGINT) or receiving SIGTERM during a parallel\n  run cancels every in-flight eval, classifies them as `INTERRUPTED`,\n  lets the orchestrator write a partial summary, and surfaces process\n  exit code `3` to the CLI shell.\n* When an individual eval exceeds its `EvalSpec.timeout_sec` budget the\n  runner kills the underlying PTY subprocess and reaps the zombie so the\n  next eval in the queue starts in a clean process table, producing an\n  `EvalOutcome` with status `TIMEOUT`.\n\nThis deliverable ships the *primitives*. Wiring the primitives into the\nCLI entrypoint (signal handler installation around the orchestrator) and\nthe partial-summary writer belongs to T03.15 / Phase 4.\n\n## 2. Public Surface\n\n```python\nfrom superclaude.cli.eval.signal_handler import (\n    EXIT_INTERRUPTED,            # int = 3\n    DEFAULT_INTERRUPT_SIGNALS,   # (SIGINT, SIGTERM)\n    CancellationToken,\n    SignalHandlerInstaller,\n)\nfrom superclaude.cli.eval.runner import EvalRunner\n```\n\n### 2.1 `CancellationToken`\n\nThread-safe cooperative cancellation flag wrapping\n`threading.Event`. One-shot: once cancelled, the token stays cancelled\nfor the rest of its lifetime; the harness allocates a fresh token per\nrun rather than resetting.\n\n| Method | Contract |\n|---|---|\n| `cancel(*, signum=None) -> bool` | Flip to cancelled. Returns `True` on the first call, `False` thereafter. First call captures `signum` (read via `.signum`); subsequent calls do **not** overwrite. |\n| `is_cancelled() -> bool` | Non-blocking poll. |\n| `wait(timeout=None) -> bool` | Blocking wait honouring `Event.wait` semantics. |\n| `.signum -> Optional[int]` | The signal number that triggered cancellation, if any. |\n\n### 2.2 `SignalHandlerInstaller`\n\nContext manager binding configured signals (default\n`SIGINT, SIGTERM`) to a handler that:\n\n1. Calls `token.cancel(signum=signum)`.\n2. Invokes the optional `on_signal(signum, frame, token)` callback.\n   Failures inside the callback are swallowed because signal handlers\n   must always return cleanly.\n\nOn `__exit__` / `restore()` the previous handlers (captured at install\ntime) are restored — installing twice is idempotent.\n\nConstraints:\n\n* Must be installed from the main thread. Off-main-thread install raises\n  `ValueError` (mirrors `signal.signal`'s own restriction).\n* Empty `signals` iterable rejected with `ValueError`.\n* `restore()` is a no-op when called without a prior `install()`.\n\n### 2.3 `EvalRunner` integration\n\n`EvalRunner.__init__` accepts a new optional kwarg\n`cancellation_token: CancellationToken | None`. When wired:\n\n| Trigger | Behaviour | Outcome |\n|---|---|---|\n| Token already cancelled at `run()` entry | Skip the lifecycle entirely; do **not** call `home.setup` or `executor.spawn`; emit `interrupted_fired` + `outcome` events; flush log. | `INTERRUPTED`, `duration_sec=0.0`, `error_class=None` |\n| Worker thread raises `KeyboardInterrupt` / `SystemExit` | Set the token (defensive) and convert into an INTERRUPTED outcome; invoke best-effort `executor.cancel()` and `home.teardown(keep=True)`; flush log. | `INTERRUPTED` |\n| Per-eval timeout expires (`thread.join(timeout)` returns alive) | Emit `timeout_fired`; invoke `executor.cancel()` from the main thread to kill the PtyDriver + reap zombie; emit `executor_cancel_*` events; run `home.teardown(keep=True)`; flush log. | `TIMEOUT`, `error_class=\"builtins.TimeoutError\"`, `duration_sec=timeout_sec` |\n\nIf `cancellation_token` is **not** wired, the pre-existing FR-LC1 /\nT03.05 contract is preserved verbatim — `KeyboardInterrupt` propagates\nto the caller (regression-tested by\n`test_keyboard_interrupt_in_expect_propagates`).\n\n`executor.cancel()` is duck-typed via `getattr(self._executor, \"cancel\", None)`:\n\n* Production executor (`ClaudeProcessAdapter` driving `PtyDriver`)\n  exposes a `cancel()` that issues `PtyDriver.terminate(force=True)`\n  followed by `close()` so the child receives SIGKILL and `wait()` reaps\n  the resulting zombie.\n* Test stubs / executors without cancellation simply omit the method;\n  the runner records an `executor_cancel_skipped` event in the JSONL log\n  and continues.\n\nAll cancel failures are swallowed: a TIMEOUT or INTERRUPTED outcome must\nalways return cleanly so the orchestrator can collect it. The error is\nrecorded as `executor_cancel_error` with `error_class` + `message`.\n\n## 3. New JSONL Events (additive)\n\nRecorded by `EvalRunner` in the per-eval JSONL log under\n`home_path/.eval-logs/<eval_id>.jsonl`. Each row preserves the\nD-0049 five-field shape (`event`, `ts_offset_sec`, `eval_id`, `step`,\n`extra`).\n\n| Event | Step | Extra fields | Emitted when |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `timeout_fired` | `\"timeout\"` | `{\"timeout_sec\": float}` | Per-eval timeout budget exceeded. |\n| `interrupted_fired` | `\"interrupt\"` | `{}` | Pre-cancelled token detected or worker `KeyboardInterrupt` / `SystemExit` observed with token wired. |\n| `executor_cancel_started` | `\"timeout\"` / `\"interrupt\"` | `{}` | Runner is about to call `executor.cancel()`. |\n| `executor_cancel_completed` | `\"timeout\"` / `\"interrupt\"` | `{}` | `cancel()` returned without raising. |\n| `executor_cancel_error` | `\"timeout\"` / `\"interrupt\"` | `{\"error_class\": str, \"message\": str}` | `cancel()` raised; failure is swallowed. |\n| `executor_cancel_skipped` | `\"timeout\"` / `\"interrupt\"` | `{\"reason\": str}` | Executor has no `cancel` method. |\n| `outcome` | `\"outcome\"` | `{\"status\": str, \"duration_sec\": float, \"error_class\": Optional[str]}` | Terminal classification (`INTERRUPTED` / `TIMEOUT` / `PASS` / `FAIL` / `ERRORED`). |\n\nExisting T03.05 events (`setup_*`, `spawn_*`, `inject_*`, `observe_*`,\n`assertion_*`, `teardown_*`) are unchanged.\n\n## 4. Exit Code Contract\n\n`EXIT_INTERRUPTED = 3` is exported so the CLI dispatcher (Phase 4) and\nthe orchestrator (T03.15) share a single source of truth. Mapping per\ndesign-spec §4:\n\n| Condition | Exit code |\n|---|---|\n| All evals PASS (or XFAIL / SKIPPED only) | 0 |\n| At least one FAIL / XPASS / TIMEOUT / ERRORED | 1 |\n| Harness setup error (schema, capability gate, scratch root) | 2 |\n| SIGINT / SIGTERM observed during a run | 3 |\n\nThis deliverable owns *only* the `EXIT_INTERRUPTED` constant + the\nCancellationToken/SignalHandlerInstaller wiring. The dispatcher that\ncalls `sys.exit(3)` lands in Phase 4.\n\n## 5. Out of Scope\n\n* **Partial-summary writing.** The reporter\n  (COMP-008 / T03.13) is responsible for persisting the interrupted run\n  summary. `SignalHandlerInstaller.on_signal` is the hook the\n  orchestrator can use to call into the reporter, but no concrete\n  writer ships here.\n* **Orchestrator wiring.** Allocating the shared `CancellationToken`,\n  installing the handler around the ThreadPoolExecutor, and translating\n  cancelled futures into outcomes belongs to T03.15.\n* **Retry policy.** NFR-REL2 (T03.08) builds on top of these\n  primitives.\n* **`signal.alarm`-based per-eval timeout.** The runner already uses a\n  `threading.Thread.join(timeout=...)` strategy (T03.05) that does not\n  hold the GIL or interfere with the main-thread signal handler.\n  Switching to `signal.alarm` would conflict with the signal handler\n  installer; we explicitly do not use it.\n\n## 6. Failure Modes & Containment\n\n* **Token cancelled mid-step.** The runner does not interrupt the\n  worker thread synchronously. The token's role is to (a) prevent the\n  orchestrator scheduling further evals and (b) let the runner detect\n  the worker's eventual `KeyboardInterrupt` / `SystemExit` and convert\n  it to `INTERRUPTED`. PtyDriver kill is the lever that actually unblocks\n  a stuck `expect()` call.\n* **Executor `cancel()` raises.** Logged as `executor_cancel_error`;\n  TIMEOUT / INTERRUPTED outcome still returns. The zombie may persist,\n  but the harness exit will reap it via the daemon-thread\n  `Thread.join` semantics.\n* **Handler called from non-main thread.** `SignalHandlerInstaller`\n  refuses to install (Python restriction); the orchestrator must\n  install before spawning worker threads.\n* **Restoration failure.** Best-effort: `signal.signal` errors during\n  `restore()` are swallowed so harness shutdown is never blocked.\n\n## 7. Without a\n  token wired, the propagation path documented by T03.05 / FR-LC1 is\n  preserved verbatim.\n\n### Why not `signal.alarm`?\n\nThe phase task wording mentions `signal.alarm` as an option.
